mapName: A Learnable North & West Asia - Identify Every Country

metas.name: Israel - Chevrons
metas.note: • Chevrons are white on black.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Israel - Curbs
metas.note:
• You will very often see striped kerbs.
  • Red and white and fairly commonly black and white.
  • Red and yellow and blue and white are also rarely found.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Israel - Gen 3 Black Car
metas.note:
• Most Generation 3 coverage was taken by a black Street View car with a long antenna.
  • You may also see the black car without an antenna and a silver car with a short antenna.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Israel - Kilometre Markers
metas.note: • Kilometre markers are white with a thick border, which can either be red, green or blue.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Israel - License Plates
metas.note:
• Israeli licence plates are yellow with a blue strip on the left.

--- NOTE:

  • While this design is specific for Israel, it is also very common on the West Bank.
  • Jordan and the UAE use white licence plates.
  • Tunisia uses black plates.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Israel - Painted Poles
metas.note: • Utility poles commonly feature these painted black and white striped bottoms.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Israel - Roadlines
metas.note: • Most roads feature yellow outer lines with white centre lines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Israel - Stop Sign
metas.note: • Rather than having a word meaning ‘stop’ written on them, stop signs have a hand painted on them.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Jordan - Architecture
metas.note:
• Most buildings in Jordan are made of bright sandstone bricks and have flat roofs.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar sandstone bricks are also common in Jerusalem.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/jordan.

metas.name: Jordan - Black Car
metas.note:
• Coverage in Jordan was taken by a black Google car, without a red brake light.

--- NOTE:

  • Jordan is the only Middle Eastern country where a black Google car without an antenna or a red brake light can be found.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/jordan.

metas.name: Jordan - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Jordanian chevrons are white with red arrows.

--- NOTE:

  • You can use chevrons to distinguish between Jordan and Israel:
  • The Israeli chevrons are black with white arrows.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/jordan.

metas.name: Jordan - License Plates
metas.note:
• Jordanian licence plates are white and can be long or short.
  • Commercial transport vehicles, such as taxis, have a distinctive green strip on the left.

--- NOTE:

  • In the Middle East, the green strip is only found in Jordan.
  • The UAE also uses long white plates.
  • Israel however only uses yellow licence plates.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/jordan.

metas.name: Jordan - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Roads in Jordan typically feature yellow outside and white middle lines.

--- NOTE:

  • Other Middle Eastern countries such as the UAE and Israel can also have these road lines.
  • Make sure to check other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/jordan.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Bollards
metas.note:
• Kazakhstan uses a variety of post-Soviet style bollards, as well as ones that resemble Turkish bollards.
  • Notably, the bollards seemingly consisting of two thin bollards attached at a 90° angle are unique to Kazakhstan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Car
metas.note: • All of the coverage in Kazakhstan was taken with a white pickup truck, which can either be fully visible or mostly blurred.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Gas Pipes
metas.note: • Gas pipes are extremely common in Kazakh cities.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Landscape
metas.note:
• Kazakhstan is a big and diverse country, which features a plethora of distinct landscapes like deserts, grassy steppes, mountain passes, and birch forests.
  • Most strikingly, most of the rural coverage in Kazakhstan is in a very empty, open and mostly flat landscape.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Pedestrian Crossing
metas.note:
• Like Russia, Kazakhstan uses yellow and white stripes on their pedestrian crossings.
  • However, unlike Russia the stripes often have white dashes on either side.
  • Sometimes, you can find the dashes without the stripes.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Russian Infrastructure
metas.note: • A lot of Kazakh infrastructure, from pedestrian signs, poles, houses, to bollards, is very similar to what you see in Russia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan.

metas.name: Kyrgyzstan - Bollards
metas.note: • Kyrgyzstan uses these simple white bollards with a diagonal black stripe near the top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kyrgyzstan.

metas.name: Kyrgyzstan - Car
metas.note:
• Kyrgyzstan can be recognised from the silver car and four bars that are visible.
  • All coverage is Generation 3.

--- NOTE:

  • No other country with a similar landscape has a similar Street View car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kyrgyzstan.

metas.name: Kyrgyzstan - Landscape
metas.note: • All of Kyrgyzstan was covered during the winter months, so many of the trees will lack leaves, the landscape will be quite drab, and you can see snow in many parts of Kyrgyzstan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kyrgyzstan.

metas.name: Kyrgyzstan - License Plates
metas.note:
• Licence plates in Kyrgyzstan have a red strip on them.

--- NOTE:

  • Licence plates with red strips can sometimes be seen in Albania and very rarely in the UAE.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kyrgyzstan.

metas.name: Mongolia - Bollards
metas.note: • Mongolia uniquely features white bowling-pin shaped bollards with two red stripes around the top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Mongolia - Cars
metas.note:
• Mongolia very often has a visible Street View car as all of Mongolian coverage was driven with a large pickup truck.
  • The truck can have several features such as a tent on top, red side-view mirrors, a snorkel, and roof-racks.
  • All of these can be of help in identifying Mongolia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Mongolia - Landscape
metas.note:
• Mongolia can typically be identified by the steppe biomes found across the country.
  • While some forested areas are found in Mongolia, most of the country features empty grasslands or deserts with a characteristic lack of trees.

--- NOTE:

  • It is not uncommon to find rugged, rocky or rolling hills as well as rivers and lakes across Mongolia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Mongolia - Round Yurts
metas.note: • White, round yurts are the traditional dwelling of nomadic families in Mongolia, and are often seen all around the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Oman - Car
metas.note: • All the coverage in Oman was taken with a white pickup truck, meaning you will either see most of the car or a large front blur.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/oman.

metas.name: Oman - Chevrons
metas.note: • Oman uses black-and-yellow chevrons that have an unusually large number of arrows.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/oman.

metas.name: Oman - Curbs
metas.note:
• Black-and-yellow curbs are common in Oman.

--- NOTE:

  • The UAE also commonly uses similar curbs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/oman.

metas.name: Oman - Garbage Bins
metas.note:
• The vast majority of garbage bins in Oman are either black and made of plastic or metallic and grey, with a three-leaf logo and the text ‘be’ah’ below it.

--- NOTE:

  • Garbage bins in the UAE will occasionally have the text “bee’ah”, with two E’s.
  • The bins are often more colourful too.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/oman.

metas.name: Oman - High Voltage Pylons
metas.note:
• High voltage pylons painted with a red and white pattern are common in Oman.

--- NOTE:

  • Within the Middle East, red and white painted pylons can also less commonly be found in Qatar.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/oman.

metas.name: Oman - Landscape
metas.note:
• Most of Oman features a desert landscape with little vegetation.
  • While the middle and southern half is mostly flat, the north coast features dry mountains similar to those found in the UAE.
  • The southern coast also has mountains, though less dry.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/oman.

metas.name: Oman - License Plates
metas.note: • Licence plates on private vehicles are generally yellow, while commercial vehicles have red plates.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/oman.

metas.name: Oman - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Roads in Oman use yellow outer and white middle lines.

--- NOTE:

  • This is also common in the UAE, Israel, Jordan, as well as occasionally found in Qatar.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/oman.

metas.name: Oman - Striped Signposts
metas.note:
• Many signposts in Oman have black-and-white stripes.

--- NOTE:

  • Within the Middle East, striped signposts are only found in Oman and the UAE.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/oman.

metas.name: Qatar - Car
metas.note:
• The Google car will usually be blurred, with only the antenna on the left and a sliver of the car visible.
  • Sometimes the entire white pickup truck can be visible.
  • Rusty clips can be seen on the crossbar.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/qatar.

metas.name: Qatar - Chevrons
metas.note: • Qatar uses white on red and white on blue chevrons.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/qatar.

metas.name: Qatar - Landscape
metas.note:
• Qatar's landscape is predominantly desert, with arid, and mostly flat expanses of sand as far as the eye can see.
  • You will often not see a lot of trees or other greenery.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/qatar.

metas.name: Qatar - License Plates
metas.note:
• Regular cars in Qatar have long, white licence plates with a maroon strip on the left.
  • Trucks have square, black licence plates and police plates are blue.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/qatar.

metas.name: Qatar - Pedestrian Sign
metas.note: • Qatari crossing signs feature a man in a thobe.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/qatar.

metas.name: Qatar - Poles
metas.note:
• Qatar uses round poles with 3 insulators on the pole top, with the middle one being slightly higher.
  • The crossbar also has 2 diagonal bars connecting it to the pole.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/qatar.

metas.name: Qatar - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Qatar typically uses solid outer white lines with either white or yellow in the middle.
  • More rarely, you can also find outer yellow lines too.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/qatar.

metas.name: Turkey - Apartment Blocks
metas.note: • Tall and somewhat square apartment blocks are very common in Turkey.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Turkey - Bollards
metas.note:
• Turkish bollards have a simple design: rectangular, plain white, and with a red reflector on the front.
  • They are thin when seen from the side.

--- NOTE:

  • Romania has similar bollards.
  • However, bollards are relatively rare in Romania.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Turkey - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Turkish chevrons are typically red on white.
  • Beware that there are some other regional variants.
  • Usually, the tip of the arrow does not touch the edge of the chevron.
  • Some chevrons have a neon yellow border.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Turkey - Gen 3 No Antenna
metas.note: • In the Generation 3 coverage, the Google car never has an antenna.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Turkey - Gen 4 Truck
metas.note:
• A grey pickup truck can be found in some Generation 4 coverage.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar pickup trucks can also be found in Senegal and Kenya.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Turkey - Gen 4 White Car
metas.note:
• The Generation 4 coverage in Turkey typically features a white Google car.
  • Usually, only a tiny sliver of the back of the car is visible.
  • The car can have a short antenna, or no antenna at all.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Turkey - Roadlines
metas.note:
• The colour of Turkish road lines is somewhat inconsistent.
  • Most roads simply have white road lines.
  • However, it is not uncommon to see yellow road lines.
  • These roads can have fully yellow lines, or a combination of yellow and white lines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Turkey - Salt & Pepper Roads
metas.note: • Many roads have pavement with a grainy “salt and pepper” texture.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Turkey - Stop Sign
metas.note:
• Stop signs have the word “DUR” written on them.
  • This is unique to Turkey.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Curbs
metas.note:
• Similarly, almost all curbs are striped.
  • They can be either black-and-white, or black-and-yellow.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Gen 3 Car
metas.note:
• In almost all Generation 3 coverage, a white car with visible black roof racks was used.

--- NOTE:

  • The UAE is the only Middle Eastern country where a white Google car can be found.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Gen 4 Black Car
metas.note:
• You can also find regular Generation 4 coverage taken with a black car.
  • The brake light is commonly visible.

--- NOTE:

  • A similar Generation 4 black car can be found in Israel.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Gen 4 Truck
metas.note:
• In Generation 4 coverage, a white pickup truck with a trekker camera was used for much of the coverage.
  • In a lot of the coverage, the truck is completely blurred out.

--- NOTE:

  • A similar truck can be found in Qatar and Oman.
  • In the UAE the antenna at the front of the cabin is on the middle of the car, while in Qatar it is on the left.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Landscape
metas.note: • The UAE typically features a flat desert landscape.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Poles
metas.note:
• Electricity poles in the UAE are mostly made of dark brown wood.
  • The pole tops consist of three insulators, symmetrically attached to a horizontal metal bar.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar poletops can be found in Oman.
  • Jordanian poletops may look similar, but they are usually made of grey concrete, and the insulators are more spaced out.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Reddish Sidewalks
metas.note:
• Houses in residential areas are typically made of light-coloured stone.
  • Reddish stones are often used for sidewalks.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Outer roadlines are yellow, middle lines either white or yellow.

--- NOTE:

  • Other Middle Eastern countries, like Jordan, Israel and Oman, also use these lines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Unpaved Roads
metas.note: • Although the UAE is a wealthy country, it is not uncommon for residential roads to be unpaved.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates.
